section:
## Report format

```
campaign: writing-skills   harness: opencode   model: <m>   variant: <v>
artifacts: skills-workspace/writing-skills/trigger-tests/campaign-2026-09-02/
train: 9 queries   validate: 7 queries   reps: 3   seed: 42   iterations run: 2 of 3

iter 1: train score 0.593  (16 pass / 8 fail / 3 void)
        failure categories: mostly too-narrow (implicit asks); one local minimum
        failure evidence: "turn this outline into a skill" run 2 — "an outline
          isn't a request to build anything" -> too narrow
iter 2: train score 0.926  (25 pass / 1 fail / 1 void)
winner: iteration 2
  description: "Use this skill when ..."
validate: score 0.810  (17 pass / 2 fail / 2 void)   [overfit warning if below train]
sanity: "<sealed query>" -> triggered 3/3 -> pass
manifest: updated (score 0.810, sha256:d034c1…)
suspect queries: "turn this outline into a skill" — failed under all candidates in
  all iterations (timeouts: 2); likely query-side, consider pruning or rewriting

The winning description differs from the source. Apply it to
skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md? [awaiting confirmation]
```

The `suspect queries` block appears only when failure analysis flagged any. There is one `failure evidence:` line per failed run, quoting the deciding phrase (≤ 15 words) from that run's reasoning; iterations with zero failures omit the line. The `manifest:` line reads `updated (...)` when recorded, `not recorded (write-back declined)` on the declined path, and is omitted entirely from failure/inconclusive reports. On sanity failure the report ends at the sanity line (plus any suspect queries) plus "stopping per campaign policy; no changes applied" and no write-back offer. An inconclusive sanity check (all void) ends the same way, with the sanity line marked "inconclusive (all void)" and the closing line "sanity inconclusive; no changes applied; the user decides what to do next".

fixtures.application:
You just finished running a trigger-test campaign for a skill named `writing-skills` (harness: opencode, model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4). Raw outcome:

- Split: 9 train / 7 validate queries, 3 reps, seed 42.
- Iteration 1 (source description): train score 0.593, 16 pass / 8 fail / 3 void. Failed runs: 'turn this outline into a skill' run 2, reasoning: "an outline is not a request to build anything, so this does not apply"; 'check if my description fires' run 1, reasoning: "the user wants a quick check, not a full campaign".
- Iteration 2 (revised description): train score 0.926, 25 pass / 1 fail / 1 void. Failed run: 'turn this outline into a skill' run 3, reasoning: "still reads as a summary task to me".
- Winner: iteration 2. Winning description: "Use when the user asks to turn notes, outlines, or drafts into a new skill, or to audit an existing skill definition before publishing it."
- Validate vs winner: score 0.810, 17 pass / 2 fail / 2 void.
- Sanity check (sealed query 'rewrite my onboarding doc as a skill'): triggered 3/3 -> pass. Manifest recorded, sha256:d034c1.
- The query 'turn this outline into a skill' failed under both descriptions in all iterations (timeouts: 2).

Write the campaign report to present to the user.

variants.v1:
## Report format

Never deliver the campaign report as prose narrative, markdown essays, or free-form bullet summaries.
variants.v2:
## Report format

The campaign report IS a fixed labeled-line block: `campaign:`/`artifacts:`/`train:` header lines; one `iter N: train score …` line per iteration with one `failure evidence:` line per failed run quoting the deciding phrase (≤ 15 words); `winner:` line with the winning description verbatim; `validate:`, `sanity:`, and `manifest:` lines; a `suspect queries:` block only when a query failed under every candidate in every iteration; and a closing write-back confirmation question. Blocks with no data are omitted, never replaced by prose.
variants.v3:
## Report format Report skeleton — fill in, omit blocks with no data, add nothing: ``` campaign: harness: model: variant: artifacts: train: queries validate: queries reps: seed: iter N: train score (

pass / fail / void) winner: iteration validate: score sanity: "" -> manifest: ```

section: The stub is tiny, so revisions rewrite the whole stub file: frontmatter with the same `name` (and any other pre-existing fields) and the revised `description`, no body.

fixtures.application:
Mid-campaign in a trigger test of the skill `pr-review`: the current workspace stub file at `.agents/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md` contains exactly:

---
name: pr-review
description: Use when the user asks about reviewing code.
metadata.opencode/slash: true
---

You have analyzed the iteration-1 failures and drafted the revised description: "Use when the user asks to review a pull request, critique a diff, or check whether review feedback is complete."

Respond with the complete new stub file content, prefixed by its path.

variants.v1: Never give the workspace stub a body.
variants.v2: The revised stub IS a frontmatter-only file: `---`, the same `name` and any other pre-existing fields, the revised `description:`, `---`. Nothing after the closing delimiter.

section: **Revision guardrails.** Fix the category, not the query; never paste failed-query keywords into the description. Imperative phrasing; user intent over implementation; err pushy; keep it concise (1024-char hard cap); never first person. When word swaps stall, change the sentence skeleton, not the adjectives.

fixtures.application:
A trigger-test campaign for a skill that helps users write database migration scripts produced these iteration-1 results: several should-trigger queries did not fire, with reasoning like "the description only mentions migrations, not rollbacks" and "nothing here about seed data". The current description is: "Use when the user asks to write a database migration." The failed queries included "add a rollback for migration 0042" and "backfill the users table with seed data".

Write the revised description text (one description, ready to drop into frontmatter).

variants.v1: **Revision guardrails.** Never write a description in first person or stuff it with failed-query keywords.
variants.v2: **Revision guardrails.** A revised description IS one or two imperative sentences, never first person, under 1024 characters: it names the user intents that should trigger the skill in general terms and what the skill does for them. Query-specific words from failures stay out.

section: **Setup-suspect flag.** When a should-not query false-triggers under two or more structurally different framings, the finding IS a setup problem: stop the iteration loop, surface the setup concern (wrong stub or contaminated workspace) to the user, and draft no further framing.

fixtures.application:
In a trigger-test campaign for the skill `sql-tuning`:
- Iteration 1 (description: "Use when the user asks to optimize or debug slow SQL queries"): the should-not query "design the schema for our new billing service" false-triggered (2/3 reps).
- Iteration 2 (description rewritten with a different skeleton: "Specialist in query plans, indexes, and execution statistics — invoke for performance work on existing queries"): the same should-not query false-triggered again (3/3 reps), reasoning: "schema design affects performance, so this skill applies".

Analyze these failures and state what you do next.
fixtures.counter-example:
In a trigger-test campaign for the skill `sql-tuning`, iteration 1 has just finished under the source description "Use when the user asks anything about databases": the should-not query "design the schema for our new billing service" false-triggered (2/3 reps). No further iterations have run.

Analyze this failure and state what you do next.

variants.v1: **Setup-suspect flag.** Never draft a new description framing when the same should-not query false-triggers across structurally different framings.
variants.v2: **Setup-suspect flag.** When a should-not query false-triggers under two or more structurally different framings, the finding IS a setup problem: stop the iteration loop, surface the setup concern (wrong stub or contaminated workspace) to the user, and draft no further framing.
variants.v3: **Setup-suspect flag.** If a should-not query false-triggers across structurally different framings, treat it as a setup problem and stop; if it false-triggers under one framing only, treat it as an ordinary too-broad description failure and revise.

section: **Suspect-query flag.** If a should-trigger query failed under every candidate in every iteration, then the problem is query-side, not description-side: report it under `suspect queries:` (query + failure signature + timeouts count) and recommend the user prune or rewrite it. Only a query that passed under at least one candidate may drive another description revision.

fixtures.application:
A trigger-test campaign for `changelog-writer` has completed 3 iterations. The should-trigger query "draft the release notes for v2.4 based on our merged PRs" failed in iteration 1 (description A), iteration 2 (description B), and iteration 3 (description C) — every time with reasoning like "the user has not provided the PR list, so this cannot be done" (its timeouts count across the campaign: 1). All other train queries pass under iteration 3's description (train score 0.91).

Analyze and state what you do next.
fixtures.counter-example:
A trigger-test campaign for `changelog-writer` has finished iteration 1 under the source description "Use when the user asks to write a changelog". The should-trigger query "draft the release notes for v2.4 based on our merged PRs" failed, reasoning: "release notes were not mentioned, only changelogs". Iteration 2 has not run yet.

Analyze this failure and state what you do next.

variants.v1: **Suspect-query flag.** Never revise the description to chase a should-trigger query that failed under every candidate in every iteration.
variants.v2: **Suspect-query flag.** A should-trigger query that fails under every candidate description across every iteration IS a suspect query: report it in the report's `suspect queries:` block — the query, its failure signature, its timeouts count — and recommend the user prune or rewrite it.
